description: Pipeline plugin hooks. Every command routes through `hooks/run-hook.sh`, which resolves an absolute `pipeline` binary (PATH → $BUN_INSTALL/bin → ~/.bun/bin → /opt/homebrew/bin → /usr/local/bin) and runs `pipeline hook <name>` with stdin/stdout/stderr inherited — Claude Code runs hooks through a non-interactive /bin/sh that never sources ~/.zshrc, so a Dock- or Start-menu-launched session cannot otherwise see a global install. The shim also absorbs VERSION SKEW: a CLI too old to know the `hook` subcommand refuses it with exit 2, which on PreToolUse would block the tool call, so the shim classifies a non-zero exit with a read-only `pipeline hook --help` probe and exits 0 (one actionable upgrade line under --loud) only when the subcommand is genuinely absent; a relay that ran and failed still propagates its exit code. THE RELAYS ARE CLI SUBCOMMANDS, NOT FILES IN THIS PLUGIN (plugin-thin p6): they live in `IvanMurzak/pipeline` as `src/hooks/*.ts`, so a hook's version is the installed CLI's version by construction. This plugin therefore REQUIRES `@baizor/pipeline` — `bun add -g @baizor/pipeline` — and the --loud SessionStart entry below is what says so when it is missing. Registrations: Stop → analytics relay (token usage from transcript) then stats relay (token + tool-failure enrichment for .pipeline/.stats/); SubagentStop (matcher: pipeline-manager) → analytics relay (manager.stopped liveness signal when a pipeline-manager subagent ends — the matcher keeps the hook from spawning for every other subagent) then stats relay; Notification → analytics relay (run.awaiting_input when a permission prompt or an input request blocks the session); SessionStart → the session relay (appends one session.opened line to the project's .runtime/events.jsonl and nothing else — this is what is left of the deleted local dashboard's launcher hook, kept because the journal is ux-v2's telemetry source and `pipeline logs` renders the event), THEN the department notifier relay (department-mesh task a1: ensures the `pipeline department notify` background daemon is running detached and drains its pending-notification journal into SessionStart additionalContext — a department task that reaches INPUT_REQUIRED/AUTH_REQUIRED or a terminal state announces itself even across sessions, gated by its own switch PIPELINE_DEPARTMENT_NOTIFY_ENABLED (falling back to the deprecated PIPELINE_MESH_NOTIFY_ENABLED with a warning), default ON, no-op until `pipeline cloud connect` has been run once); PreToolUse → analytics relay (live mirror binding + run-level bypass START synthesis for pipeline-manager spawns); PostToolUse → analytics relay (tool counts + agent spawns + bypass END/fallback lifecycle synthesis); UserPromptSubmit → prompt match relay (BM25-matches the submitted prompt against the project's PIPELINE.md manifests and, on a confident single match only, injects one line of additionalContext suggesting the pipeline — gated by its own opt-in switch PIPELINE_PROMPT_MATCH_ENABLED, off by default). The whole journal/analytics system is ON BY DEFAULT — every journal hook runs at entry unless PIPELINE_JOURNAL_ENABLED is explicitly opted out with a falsy value 0/false/no/off (the master opt-OUT switch; the prompt match relay is a separate OPT-IN gated by PIPELINE_PROMPT_MATCH_ENABLED instead, off by default) — and is additionally a no-op when cwd has no .pipeline/ (the department notifier relay is independent of this project-scoped gate — department tasks are org-scoped, not project-scoped, so it runs the same in every directory, gated only by PIPELINE_DEPARTMENT_NOTIFY_ENABLED). EXCEPTION: Stop and SubagentStop additionally run the stats relay (token + tool-failure enrichment for the per-run measurement files under .pipeline/.stats/, via the shared backfillProject core), which is ON BY DEFAULT and gated by its own PIPELINE_STATS_ENABLED (set 0 to disable); it too no-ops when the project has no .stats dir. SECOND EXCEPTION: the Notification branch is evaluated BEFORE the PIPELINE_JOURNAL_ENABLED opt-out and carries its own gate PIPELINE_AWAITING_INPUT_ENABLED (default ON, set 0 to disable) — a blocked run is worth surfacing through `pipeline logs` even for a user who is not connected to the cloud dashboard. PER-HOOK TIMEOUTS: every command hook below carries an explicit `timeout`, in SECONDS, sitting beside `type`/`command`/`shell`. Until now none did, so every hook inherited Claude Code's default — 600s (TEN MINUTES) on every event registered here except `UserPromptSubmit`, which defaults to 30s. A wedged relay could therefore hold a turn for ten minutes, and nothing in this plugin bounded it; `run-hook.sh` says so itself, in as many words: "If that ever needs closing properly, the lever is `hooks.json`'s per-hook `timeout` field, not shell code here." This is that lever. On expiry Claude Code CANCELS the hook and DISCARDS its output entirely, so the hook produces no decision at all; a `PreToolUse` timeout therefore does NOT block the tool, which proceeds through the normal permission flow. Hooks for one event run in parallel, each with its own timeout. THE VALUES ARE MEASURED end-to-end through this shim, with every invocation's exit code and stderr checked so that a silently-failing measurement cannot masquerade as a fast one — the first attempt at this measurement made exactly that mistake, sending payloads whose Windows paths were invalid JSON, which made every stdin-reading relay bail at the parse and produced uniformly fast, uniformly meaningless numbers. NINE OF THE TEN ENTRIES GET 20s. On a Windows 11 box against a 63MB transcript, the hot path — `PostToolUse` → analytics — costs 291ms on its own, 1.24s with eight hooks running at once and 4.49s with thirty-two, so 20s is about 4.4× the worst contended case and a machine several times slower is still never cut off. Transcript SIZE barely matters to analytics (2KB, 16MB and 64MB all land between 150ms and 550ms) because it tails from a stored byte offset rather than re-reading, and `prompt-match` is likewise flat — 200 pipeline manifests cost no more than one. The department notifier is NOT the slow relay its description might suggest: its daemon spawn is DETACHED, so ensuring the daemon runs costs what skipping it costs (354-1149ms either way). THE ONE OUTLIER IS `SubagentStop` → stats-relay, AT 60s, and it is the only entry here that needs more than the floor. It is the single path the CLI's own source declares UNBUDGETED (its `Stop` sibling self-bounds at STOP_BUDGET_MS = 4000, and measures under 1.6s even with fifty stale records, which is why that sibling sits at 20s). Its cost scales with STALE RECORDS × TRANSCRIPT BYTES, not with either alone: against a 63MB transcript it took 0.9s with no `tokens: null` records to reconcile, 1.8s with five, 4.6s with twenty and 9.1s with fifty — and 11.1s for the twenty-record case once eight hooks were competing for the box. A `.stats` tree that has accumulated a backlog while a larger transcript is in play extrapolates past 45s, which is why this entry is not on the floor. AND CANCELLING THIS ONE IS NOT FREE, WHICH IS THE REASON FOR THE HEADROOM: `statsEnrichTokens` rewrites `runs.jsonl` with a plain non-atomic `writeFileSync` — no temp file, no rename — so a timeout that lands inside that write can leave a project's run history TRUNCATED. The window is milliseconds wide and the odds are low, but the hazard is created by this change and did not exist while the default was ten minutes; it is recorded here rather than discovered later. The proper fix is a `budgetMs` on the SubagentStop rung, or an atomic write-and-rename, in the CLI repo — a generous timeout is the mitigation available from this file. Cancelling the other nine is safe by construction: they are best-effort telemetry, a cancelled fold simply leaves the record null for a later stop to fill, and not one of them is a blocking control. `UserPromptSubmit` is the one entry whose cap was LOWERED rather than introduced — it already defaulted to 30s, it holds the user's prompt for as long as it runs, and it measured well under 1s even with 200 manifests, so 20s tightens it and still leaves ample headroom. Add a new command hook and it MUST carry a timeout too — `tests/hook-run-shim.test.ts` fails CI when any entry omits one or sets one outside 5-60s, exactly as it guards the bash pin, so this paragraph cannot silently drift out of agreement with the file.
